subject: Proposal — level slope & local market anchors
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, comp@mercer.com, hello@talentops.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal — level slope & local market anchors

Team,

Attached is a first-pass proposal for a small, targeted update to our compensation bands focused on two things:
1) smoothing the level-to-level salary slope for IC3–IC5 so the step increases better reflect scope progression, and
2) tightening geo anchors (US coastal / US midwest / EU west / APAC) to reduce local offer variance for like-for-like roles.

What I put in the spreadsheet (redwood_comp_band_raw_v1.xlsx) is intentionally conservative — the idea is to align median anchors to updated benchmarking (Mercer) and then apply a ~5–7% slope compression between adjacent levels where we currently see large step-ups that are causing volatility in offers.

Key asks:
- Laura / Mina: can you review the proposed level slopes and note any major retention risks (esp. EMEA senior ICs)?
- Vivek: does this approach match the high-level direction we discussed in leadership sync (reduce offer churn while preserving comp pool for top performers)?
- Mercer / TalentOps: please review the attached benchmarking summary and indicate any outliers or methodology caveats (merc_benchmark_2026.pdf).

I also attached a short doc (comp-band-slopes-proposal.docx) that outlines rollout sequencing and suggested communication to hiring managers. Proposed timing: present to Exec comp committee on 11/24, implement adjusted anchors for offers starting 12/15 (subject to approvals).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Talent & Recruiting
Redwood Inference
Attach: redwood_comp_band_raw_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 420KB), merc_benchmark_2026.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB), comp-band-slopes-proposal.docx (docx, 120KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal — level slope & local market anchors

Marissa — thanks for the packet, good work pulling the pieces together. A few quick notes after skimming the workbook: 

- On the IC3→IC4 slope: your proposed 6% step-down makes sense for new hires, but we should preserve ability to grant mid-cycle adjustments for high-impact IC3s being promoted. Recommend adding a discretionary overlap buffer (2–3%) for promotions.
- EMEA: the Mercer medians you used look fine, but note the London median includes fintech comps that skew the top quartile. For our roles, consider using "EU West (tech median)" rather than "UK all industries".
- Communication: please include a short FAQ for hiring managers re: how to position offers that fall above the new median (i.e., performance-based exceptions).

I highlighted a few cells in the workbook and added comments. If we can get a revised sheet by 11/18 I can prep the Exec slide set.

On retention risks — Mina, can you run a one-week query on our voluntary exits in last 18 months for IC4–IC5 and flag any hot teams? Would like that to feed the committee.

Thanks,
Laura

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Proposal — level slope & local market anchors

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks for sharing the workbook and context. We completed a light review and attached a short note (merc_benchmark_2026.pdf) summarizing methodology caveats and recommended anchor adjustments. High level observations: 

- Our data supports tightening US coastal anchors by ~3–4% versus your current medians given the faster tech uplift in SF/NYC.
- EU West: agree with Laura — exclude cross-industry outliers and use tech-specific medians for mid-senior engineering roles. That reduces the top quartile you were seeing by ~6%.
- Slope guidance: for IC3→IC4 and IC4→IC5 a 5% compression reduces offer churn but may compress total comp for high-performing IC5s; recommend keeping a separate high-performer band (stretch band) for top 5–7% of performers.

We also attached two sample anchor tables (in the PDF) that reflect: (A) conservative adjustment (low execution risk) and (B) aggressive adjustment (faster convergence to market medians). We recommend going with (A) for the initial rollout and revisiting after 3 months of offer data.

If useful, we can run a short offer simulation against your ATS data to estimate 90-day offer acceptance delta. That would be an add-on but should be quick (2–3 business days).

Best,
Jin Park
Principal, Market Analytics — Mercer Compensation
Attach: merc_benchmark_2026.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, comp@mercer.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal — level slope & local market anchors

Thanks everyone — good analysis and clear recommendations. A few decisions from Exec: 

1) Move forward with the conservative Mercer anchor adjustments (option A).
2) Adopt the 5% slope compression for IC3→IC5 as the default, with the documented discretionary overlap buffer (2–3%) for promotions and a separate stretch band for top performers.
3) Mina / HR Ops to run the voluntary-exits pull and a one-week offer-simulation; results due 11/30.
4) Launch communication with hiring managers on 12/01 and apply new anchors to new offers effective 12/15.

Marissa — please update the slides and workbook per Laura's redlines and Mercer option A. After the update, route the final packet to me and I will sign the Exec approval memo. Also include an estimate of the near-term budget impact (headcount × average delta) — finance will need that for December planning.

Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference
